 Subscribe SEPANG, Oct 31 — Jorge Martin’s world championship hopes took a big hit today when he was ruled out of the Malaysian MotoGP sprint and main race with a broken wrist.
 The Spaniard arrived in Kuala Lumpur with a fracture from last weekend’s Australian Grand Prix sprint race.
 The Aprilia rider came through unscathed in yesterday’s first practice session at Sepang but then only managed a limited number of laps in the afternoon and on today morning.
 He did not come out for qualifying and said of the impact on his title hopes: “For for sure I will fight till the end, not only for me, because at the end of the day I’m already a champion, but for my team, for my people, I will fight till the end.”
 The 2024 champion’s premature exit is a huge boost to current leader and reigning champion Marc Marquez of Ducati.
 Marquez leads his fellow Spaniard Martin by 10 points in the championship with three race weekends left after this.
 Martin is now in a race to be ready to compete in Qatar next weekend.
 “We’ve decided to withdraw (him) from the rest of the weekend,” said Aprilia Racing team manager Paolo Bonora.
 “He couldn’t put any force into the bike in the braking areas.
 “He’ll return to Spain and assess the Qatar GP in the coming days.” — AFP
